text: Then one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and said to me: "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who is seated on many waters.
With her the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and those who dwell on the earth grew drunk on the wine of her immorality."
And he carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness. There I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast that was covered with blasphemous names and had seven heads and ten horns.
The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls, and in her hand she held a golden cup full of abominations and the filth of her immorality.
On her forehead was written a name, a mystery: "Babylon the Great, the mother of prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth."
And I saw that the woman was drunk with the blood of God's holy people and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. When I saw her, I was utterly astonished.

versions.text: And I saw that the woman was drunk with the blood of the saints, the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. When I saw her, I was utterly astonished.
versions.explanation: The Greek repeats the preposition with a connecting 'and' (καὶ ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος), which the current rendering drops, producing an appositional reading that merges two distinct groups. Restoring the conjunction keeps the two phrases parallel as in the source.

text: But the angel said to me: "Why are you astonished? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, the beast with the seven heads and the ten horns.

The beast you saw was, and is not, and is about to rise from the abyss and go to destruction. And those who dwell on the earth, whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, will be astonished when they see the beast, because it was, and is not, and yet will come.
This calls for a mind with wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman is seated. They are also seven kings:

versions.text: This calls for a mind with wisdom. The seven heads are seven hills on which the woman is seated. They are also seven kings:
versions.explanation: ὄρη normally means 'mountains'; 'hills' imports an interpretive allusion to Rome's seven hills. 'Mountains' is the more literal rendering and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: five have fallen, one is, the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain only a little while.
As for the beast that was and is not, it is itself an eighth, and yet it belongs to the seven, and it goes to destruction.
The ten horns you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, but they will receive authority as kings for one hour, together with the beast.
These are of one mind, and they hand over their power and authority to the beast.
They will wage war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because he is Lord of lords and King of kings — and those with him are called, chosen, and faithful."
Then he said to me: "The waters you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and languages.

versions.text: Then he said to me: "The waters you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples and crowds and nations and languages.
versions.explanation: ὄχλοι in this fourfold formula denotes vast throngs of humanity; 'multitudes' conveys the scale better than 'crowds' and matches the elevated liturgical rhythm of the list.

text: And the ten horns you saw, together with the beast, will hate the prostitute. They will leave her desolate and naked, devour her flesh, and burn her with fire.
For God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose: to act with one mind and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.

versions.text: For God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose: to be of one mind and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.
versions.explanation: The Greek uses the verb ποιῆσαι ('to do/carry out') with μίαν γνώμην, expressing united action, not merely a shared state of mind; 'to act with one mind' preserves the verbal force and echoes the preceding 'carry out'.

text: And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth."
